Privacy notice

What personal data Week2Speak collects, why, who else handles it, how long we keep it, and the rights you have.

Last updated 18 November 2026

Who we are

Week2Speak is run by Mei Gabriela Parrablanco, a sole trader in the United Kingdom, who is the data controller for the personal data described here. Contact us about anything in this notice at hello@week2speak.com.

The short version

  • You can practise without an account: your progress then stays in your browser only.
  • If you create an account, we keep your name, email, progress and how much you use each tool, so you lose nothing and the free limits work.
  • We use one cookie, the one that keeps you signed in. No advertising or analytics cookies, and we do not track you across other websites.
  • We record calls only if you say yes, and ask separately before using any clip publicly.
  • We do not sell your data.

Recordings and clips

Before your first call we ask two separate questions, and neither is ticked for you:

  1. May we record your calls so you and Mei can hear your progress?
  2. May we use short clips of you on our website or social media?

You can agree to the first and not the second, or to neither. You can change your mind at any time by messaging Mei or emailing hello@week2speak.com. If you withdraw permission for clips, we stop using them and remove the ones we control.

Cookies and browser storage

If you sign in, we set one cookie, w2s_s, that keeps you signed in for 30 days. It is strictly necessary, does nothing else and is removed when you sign out. The site also keeps your progress, your before-and-after recordings, your language and, without an account, the daily usage counter in your browser's local storage. We use no analytics or advertising trackers.

Who else handles your data

We use a small number of providers. Each one handles your data only to provide its service to us.

Some of these providers process data outside the UK and the European Economic Area, including in the United States. Where they do, they rely on legal safeguards such as standard contractual clauses or the UK-US data bridge.

How long we keep it

  • Your account and progress: while you have the account. You can delete it yourself in Your account, and everything goes at once.
  • Unused accounts: deleted after 24 months without a sign-in.
  • Mei's notes, messages and call recordings: up to 12 months after your Sprint.
  • Clips you agreed to publish: until you withdraw permission.
  • Payment and tax records: as long as UK tax law requires, currently at least 5 years.

Your rights

Under UK and EU data protection law (UK GDPR and the GDPR) you can ask us to:

  • give you a copy of the personal data we hold about you;
  • correct data that is wrong or incomplete;
  • delete your data;
  • restrict or object to how we use it;
  • give you your data in a format you can take elsewhere;
  • withdraw any consent you gave, at any time, without affecting what we did before.

Learners in Mexico have the rights of access, rectification, cancellation and opposition under Mexico's Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties. Learners in Colombia can know, update and correct their data and revoke their authorisation under Law 1581 of 2012.

To use any of these rights, email hello@week2speak.com. We reply within one month. It is free.

Complaints

If you are unhappy with how we handle your data, please contact us first so we can put it right. You can also complain to a data protection authority:

  • United Kingdom: Information Commissioner's Office, ico.org.uk
  • Spain: Agencia Española de Protección de Datos, aepd.es
  • Colombia: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio, sic.gov.co
  • Mexico: the federal authority responsible for personal data protection

Age

Week2Speak is for adults aged 18 and over. We do not knowingly collect data from anyone younger.

Changes to this notice

If we change how we use your data, we update this page and the date at the top. If a change affects you as a learner, we tell you directly before it applies.
